cohort: The study included all women (n=139) scheduled for Caesarean delivery over a 4-month period, with 70 receiving continuous wound infusion catheters and 69 in a control group.
finding: The addition of continuous wound infusion catheters to a multimodal analgesia regimen for post-Caesarean delivery pain management showed minimal clinically significant analgesic benefits, although satisfaction scores at 24 hours were higher with the catheters.
mod_finding: For women undergoing Caesarean delivery, continuous wound infusion catheters did not significantly reduce postoperative opioid consumption or pain scores (except 24h resting pain scores) but did increase patient satisfaction at 24 hours.
